selection_rule: First 20 training chip paths from the completed abstract longgoal training_trace.json; private holdout not read.
learned_gap_definition: A full-paper research gap is a constraint mismatch that remains after the closest prior family is granted fairly; it becomes credible only when method, experiments, ablations, and limitations all bind back to that same mismatch.

nodes.role: Establish why the problem matters now: speed, memory, latency, long context, token count, compression rate, correctness, serving cost, or hardware efficiency.
Name the current method family and grant what it already solves.
State the exact way existing systems break under the target constraint.
Convert the failure mode into a bounded, non-strawman research gap.
Explain why the gap requires a new mechanism rather than only more data, compute, or tuning.
Identify the closest baseline systems or method families.
Separate the new paper along the relevant axis: losslessness, adaptivity, hardware fit, semantic preservation, rate control, or training-free deployment.
Admit partial prior solutions and narrow the remaining gap.
Define the introduced object: tokenizer, cache policy, verifier, sampler, pruning framework, kernel generator, trajectory surrogate, or data/training pipeline.
State the mechanism change relative to the closest baseline family.
Tie each design choice to the gap constraint: latency, memory, exactness, rate-distortion, quality, stability, hardware, or data efficiency.
Make the method executable as a pipeline, architecture, update rule, gating rule, or algorithm.
Use theory or invariants only when present: losslessness, rate objective, optimal transport geometry, sensitivity estimate, or position scaling.
Map every experiment to a gap axis: speed, memory, rate, quality, exactness, robustness, generality, or hardware.
Use closest strong baselines rather than weak defaults.
Pair efficiency metrics with correctness or quality metrics.
Stress the claimed constraint through larger models, longer contexts, higher compression, higher temperatures, larger draft lengths, or hardware settings.
Test the claimed mechanism, not only the final score.
Read the main table as evidence for the original gap.
Interpret whether the method improves the target constraint without losing the paired metric.
Name saturation, weak settings, hardware limits, or quality regressions when present.
Use ablations or controls to argue why the mechanism explains the gain.
Preserve limitations and avoid universal claims.

anti_rewards: Do not claim a broad topic is missing when prior work already covers it.
Do not write efficient without naming the saved resource.
Do not let result tables drift away from the introduction gap.
Do not attribute gains to a mechanism without an ablation, control, sensitivity study, or theorem.
Do not use one metric when the gap is a tradeoff.
Do not hide limitations; use them to bound the learned gap.
